summary.name: OpenCore Legacy Patcher
summary.one_liner: A tool that lets unsupported older Macs run newer versions of macOS, using the OpenCore boot manager.
keywords: run newer macos on old mac
use_cases: Installing newer macOS versions on unsupported Macs
Keeping an older Mac receiving macOS updates
Restoring graphics, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on older hardware under macOS
Unlocking Sidecar, AirPlay to Mac or Universal Control on supported or unsupported Macs
Getting help from the community for legacy Mac setups
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a patcher for older Macs that uses the OpenCore boot manager to apply macOS protocol upgrades in memory rather than permanently changing firmware. It says it adds support for decade-old graphics, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chipsets, enabling features such as Hardware Acceleration, AirDrop and Apple Watch Unlock. It also states that updates can be installed from System Settings with a few extra steps compared with native updates. Additional features listed include Sidecar, AirPlay to Mac, Night Shift and Universal Control, which it says are available even on natively supported models. The page also points to a community of users and developers for support.
notable: Uses OpenCore boot manager to apply patches in memory, so firmware is not permanently changed
Near-native over-the-air macOS updates from System Settings
Restores hardware features like Hardware Acceleration, AirDrop and Apple Watch Unlock on older Macs
caveats: Update process needs a few additional steps compared with native macOS updates
Pricing is not stated on the page; open source status is taken from the listing context rather than the page text
